findings.summary: The bullet's trigger leaves out "understand", which criterion 1 names ("know, understand or act on"). This may cause a criterion-1 mismatch at verification.
findings.evidence: Criterion 1 says: "when a request says Athena or its agents should know, understand or act on something". The draft says: "If Athena or agents should know or act on X". By my count the draft is 229 bytes with its newline, the line-6 trim saves 22, and the net is +207. That is against roughly 213–216 bytes of headroom, because 1929 tokens means 5785–5787 bytes under ⌈bytes/3⌉. Adding ", understand" (12 bytes) would overrun unless something else is cut. Fix: Use "know, understand or act on X" and pay for it by cutting other words. For example, drop "the " before "roles" (4 bytes) and shorten "name the roles and prompts changed" to "name roles and prompts changed". Alternatively, say in D170 that "know" deliberately covers "understand" for budget reasons, so the verifier sees the departure was intended.
findings.location: Plan decision 1 / step 1, drafted bullet text

findings.summary: The trigger only fires on "should know or act on X". The second introspection's proposed trigger was broader ("a request changes what a role should decide or do"), so some misreadings in this class may get past the new rule.
findings.evidence: Introspection 20261109-125651-wz8f proposed: "When a request changes what a role should decide or do, the reading step must list the rules that bound that role's actions". Job 20261109-080220-zkhy was a steward-decision change. Its wording may not have contained "know". Fix: Where it fits the budget, word the trigger to include requests that change what a role decides or does (for example "If Athena, its agents or a role should know, act on or decide X"). Otherwise, note the narrower trigger as a tradeoff in D170.

summary: I read the snapshot to check this round-2 plan; I did not run any tests. The plan puts the fix where the reading put it: one bullet under 'Reading the request' in crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md, which reading.rs:231 composes into the reader's system prompt. Every file and function it names exists, as the snapshot shows: READER_FRAME at lib.rs:38, compose at lib.rs:142, FRAME_ANCHORS at lib.rs:563 with its check at lib.rs:643, budgets.rs, the 'prompt structure' and 'decision entries' mirror rules, and D169 as the last decision, so D170 is correct. The headings '## Reading the request' and '## Forecasts' each appear once and only in reader.md, so the planned test's section slice is well defined. The test reads the real composed prompt, not a double, and none of its phrases ('docs or agent behavior', 'admission', 'blocking non-owner-only rules', and the rest) appear in the current file, so it fails before the change. By my own count the new bullet is 229 bytes with its newline and the trim saves 22, a net of +207 bytes against about 213–216 bytes of headroom, so it fits. The new bullet has no mid-line '- ' and no colon within its first 40 characters, so mirrors.rs `glued_item` will not flag it. A grep found no reader of 'Users write lazily' or 'Recover what they left unsaid'. Updating docs/system-facts.md is a forced consequence of `system_facts_budgets_match_computed`, as Athena's finding notes. The dependents list covers the readers I found. The run_pin and briefs headroom rows compute sizes live, and the prompts/reader.md string in reading.rs:6198 is an unrelated path fixture. On soundness, a prose rule with a test of the composed prompt is the approach the accepted reading fixed, and it is not a crude heuristic. I found two minor wording issues: the trigger leaves out 'understand', which criterion 1 names, and it is narrower than the second introspection's 'changes what a role should decide or do'.
